character_facts: Aghora is portrayed as a formidable warrior who refuses imperial command and fights alone.
Aghora remains loyal to a code identified as Bushitaka when an enemy attempts surrender.
Aghora is capable of destroying a universe-scale foe.
Aghora feels deep sadness after killing Deyanira and resolves to create life.
Deyanira is both a deadly companion beast and a victim of a fatal brain tumor.
Tonto is presented as someone able to diagnose Deyanira's condition.
The Technopope is important enough to be named in the recap and is killed by Deyanira.
continuity_links: This page explicitly recaps earlier issues before the current story begins.
It establishes Aghora's recent status: decorated after a major victory, grieving Deyanira, and hiding on Flos while pregnant.
The small portraits at the bottom appear to reference recurring cast members connected to the recap and upcoming story.
dialogue_meaning: The page is expository recap text rather than scene dialogue.
It recounts Aghora's origin, military conflict, destruction of a universe-scale enemy, the death of Deyanira, and Aghora's decision to conceive a child in hiding.
lore_facts: Aghora is the daughter of Steelhead.
Aghora has a female body but carries the brain of a siamese twin brother.
Aghora's breasts were altered so they would never grow, allowing Aghora to live as a male.
The Empire can formally recognize or assign status through the Imperial Court.
The Metabaron can be withheld from imperial military action under disputed circumstances.
Aghora possesses a psycho-mimetic aura and can mount a spirit attack.
An enemy can exist as the nucleus of an entire universe.
The Pluri-Galactic Medallion is an imperial award.
Flos is described as a garden planet.
plot_events: Aghora is identified as Steelhead's daughter and described as having her dead twin brother's brain in a female body altered to live as a male.
The Imperial Court delays Aghora's recognition for years, then fails to summon Aghora when an alien threat invades the universe.
Aghora goes to the Golden Planet to learn why the Metabaron was not asked for help, and is mocked at the Imperial Court for being a woman.
Imperial troops attempt to rape Aghora, but Aghora lets the tarantuwolf Deyanira destroy the attackers.
Aghora rejects command of the Imperial fleet and confronts the enemy alone.
The enemy fleet is protected by mirror-like counterattacks that reflect assaults back at Aghora's ships.
Using a psycho-mimetic aura, Aghora penetrates the enemy defenses and launches a spirit attack after facing a reflection of the self.
The enemy is revealed as the nucleus of an entire universe; Aghora destroys it, wiping out that universe.
At an award ceremony, Deyanira is overtaken by savage fury and eats the Technopope alive.
Tonto determines that Deyanira has a brain tumor that will kill the creature painfully.
Aghora mercy-kills Deyanira and, through grief, realizes a desire to create life rather than only death.
Aghora decides to have a child, extracts male cells from the brother's brain tissue in the self, impregnates the self, and hides on the garden planet Flos to give birth in peace.
